key_insight: The paper argues that for auditable hypothesis-driven decisions, output discipline and structured reasoning matter more than raw model scale, and a falsification-guided protocol can expose and control that weakness.
engineering_relevance: A model-agnostic closed-loop protocol can make LLM decision pipelines more reliable and machine-checkable, especially when outputs must be auditable and evidence-linked.
method: Formalize decision making as a five-stage closed loop.
Use a candidate × evidence matrix to falsify every candidate against every evidence item.
Require at least half of candidates to be rejected before a conclusion is emitted in a single-line verifiable format.
evidence_signal: On TCMEval-SDT (200 cases), the protocol improved weak-discipline models such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash by about +0.27, cut Kimi K3 run-to-run standard deviation from 0.218 to 0.007, and showed mixed or negative effects on already disciplined models.
watch_item: The protocol can hurt models that already have strong output discipline, so deployment should be gated by benchmarked discipline/variance rather than assumed universally beneficial.
paper_title: Output Discipline Sets the Floor: A Falsification-Guided, Model-Agnostic Agent Protocol for Auditable Hypothesis-Driven Decision Making
